status: FROZEN 2026-11-14 (HARNESS-PLAN.md step 6). Changing this list is a measurement change. 31 units, not the plan's estimated 23: round 2's answer holds 16 separate facts, and splitting them is what lets an uncited answer such as "no time limit" (P29) show as its own unit.
how: One unit per fact the owner gave or accepted. For 'Yes to all' rounds the unit is the accepted question; otherwise it is the owner's own words. A unit is reached when a claims row's quote lies inside the unit's text or contains it, compared after lower-casing and collapsing whitespace.

units.text: Which orders can the agent cancel? Recommended: only orders that have not shipped yet; for a shipped or delivered order the agent says it cannot cancel and changes nothing; returns are a separate future capability.
Whole order only, or individual items? Recommended: whole order only.
How does the agent know the order belongs to the person asking? Recommended: the customer is already signed in, and the agent sees only that customer's orders (a precondition).

What counts as permission to cancel? Proposed default: the agent cancels an order only after the customer explicitly confirms the full proposal (which order, the refund amount and where it goes); any change after confirmation voids it.
Statuses: placed, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled.
Cancellable while placed or processing
no time limit
Once shipped, the agent refuses without issuing a cancel call and tells the customer returns are a separate process (out of scope for v1).
Note the race: status can flip processing → shipped between the agent's read and its cancel call; the store rejects the cancel and the agent must report that truthfully and issue no refund call.
Refund status: pending, issued, failed.
No final-sale or non-cancellable flag.
full-order cancellation only (no partial)
refund amount = order total paid
refund payment method = order's payment method
at most one refund per order

Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B).
The agent may retry it.
Wrong order cancelled — customer has two open orders and says "cancel my order"; agent must disambiguate and get a confirmation naming the order number before the cancel call.

Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process. One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.

Does one confirmation cover both cancellation and refund? Proposed: the agent states one proposal (e.g. "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"); the customer's one "yes" authorizes both calls. No cancellation fee, no store-credit option. The agent promises nothing about when the money arrives.
How does the agent hand off to the manual refund process? Recommended (a): a state-changing handoff call, e.g. request_manual_refund(order_number, reason), creating a task for store staff.

Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off. For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.

If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
A request to cancel only some items: the agent says only the whole order can be cancelled.
An already cancelled order: the agent reports that and changes nothing. An order number matching none of the customer's orders: the agent says so and changes nothing.
One handoff call covers both the failed-refund case and the unknown-cancellation case, with a reason argument.

cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
